claims.text: A model combining CALPHAD thermodynamic inputs with machine learning can accurately identify HEAs with low phonon thermal conductivity.
CALPHAD can provide thermodynamic and phase-equilibrium information for multicomponent alloy design.
Machine learning tailored to atomic disorder can quantify the effect of disorder on phonon scattering.
High configurational complexity in HEAs causes significant phonon scattering through atomic mass variance and lattice distortions.
Compositional complexity creates variable local bonding environments.
Variable local bonding environments increase phonon scattering.
Increased phonon scattering reduces the phonon mean free path.
A reduced phonon mean free path lowers phonon thermal conductivity.
Quantifying disorder-mediated phonon scattering with CALPHAD and machine learning improves material identification over conventional empirical approaches.
Below approximately 500 °C, phonon transport is the dominant thermal-transport mechanism for the target alloys.
The approach applies to stable, single-phase, compositionally disordered HEAs without major secondary-phase precipitation.
HEAs can decompose from an initially single-phase state into multiphase microstructures during annealing.
The model may not be valid for multiphase or nanostructured composites because additional phonon-scattering mechanisms become important.
Conventional rule-of-mixtures or standard CALPHAD predictions do not account for enhanced phonon scattering caused by high atomic disorder in HEAs.
HEAs selected by the proposed model will have measured phonon thermal conductivity approximately 20–30% below conventional predictions.
The predicted 20–30% improvement is based on theoretical phonon-scattering considerations.
Exact performance and compositional limits require experimental calibration.
Nanoscale heterogeneities and processing-induced defects may affect model predictions but have not been rigorously quantified.
Time-domain thermoreflectance or inelastic neutron scattering can be used to assess phonon thermal transport in the proposed benchmark.
